{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABZc1rgw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhDEDV4", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 37, "title": "Implement the LCD one-line shade and color output delay", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `3869f9e63a853bf75825c504c448fb0be8084fdf`, `video.rs` composes pixels and immediately converts them to RGBA using current registers/RAM. `Machine::run_frame` renders the current row at its line end. The renderer explicitly omits the LCD output pipeline, and `lcd_tests.rs:352` asserts immediate whole-line recoloring.

The documented hardware delays final shade/color translation by one line relative to DISPLAY_LINE. Raster palette changes therefore affect the wrong output row. This affects monochrome rendering throughout the family and Color/Crystal color rendering; commercial-title impact remains unmeasured.

## Expected outcome

Separate line composition from final shade/color translation. During normal full-height frames, translation while DISPLAY_LINE is L applies to composed row L−1. Preserve pixel identities and composition decisions across that delay instead of shifting completed RGBA rows or refetching the previous row from changed tile/map/sprite data.

Implement this focused pipeline through the existing core and native/Wasm/browser paths, with explicit limits for unresolved timing.

## Context

Local HEAD is clean and matches remote main. The open Issue/PR collection is empty. Closed [Issue #27](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/issues/27) established programmable raster timing and explicitly deferred the full output pipeline.

Correction record: the old AI-authored assumption allowed current-line state to produce final RGBA immediately. The corrected requirement separates composition from translation one line later, following the DISPLAY_LINE documentation in the [pinned Wonderful display definitions](https://github.com/WonderfulToolchain/hardware-definitions/blob/46783132a59e576c11456f5997620594eca1c390/target/wswan/display.xml). This corrects the row targeted by software changing shade LUT or color palette values.

That source establishes the line offset, not exact fetch phases, write boundaries, or every runtime-mode transition. Inspected pinned ares PPU/screen/DAC sources provide implementation context, not independent proof of those details. WSdev Display/IO Ports returned 403, and WSman returned 502; indexed excerpts were not accepted as established requirements.

Relevant paths include `crates/ws-core/src/{video.rs,lib.rs,bus.rs,lcd_tests.rs}`, native integration tests, fixture tooling and existing browser compatibility scripts. Necessary cross-file work belongs in this task; unrelated CPU timing, OAM-copy accuracy, LCD icons and analog panel simulation remain separate gaps.

[Saved #35 validation](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/3869f9e63a853bf75825c504c448fb0be8084fdf/docs/issue-35-validation.md) reports 104 core unit tests, 15 integration tests, one adapter test, fixture/build checks and both Chromium suites passing, plus Coordinator acceptance review. Those are reported results; this planning task inspected code and evidence without running builds or tests.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Complete bounded source reconciliation before implementation: identify composition versus translation state, including monochrome palette-to-shade lookup, shade LUT, color palette RAM, backdrop, LCD enable and runtime modes. Establish the normal L→L−1 mapping from inspected technical evidence. Document unresolved sampling/latching details as explicit compatibility policies with consistency tests; do not invent hardware precision or defer the documented delay.
- [ ] Implement delayed final translation for monochrome modes on all three models and supported 2bpp/4bpp planar/packed color modes on Color/Crystal. Preserve composed pixel identities and layer/sprite priority across the delay. Subsequent tile/map/OAM changes must not recompute a pending row; palette changes must affect the appropriate translation stage. Merely delaying completed RGBA is insufficient.
- [ ] Add independent deterministic vectors distinguishing composition changes from final translation changes. Check shade-LUT and RGB12 palette writes made after composition, exact affected/adjacent rows and literal expected pixels. Include backgrounds, overlapping layers, transparency and sprites. Replace the immediate-rendering assertion with evidence-derived expectations while retaining its programmable-raster regression purpose. Demonstrate that the current immediate renderer fails the new delay checks.
- [ ] Cover row 0, row 143 translated during line 144, repeated frames, VBlank/OAM-latch ordering, and normal totals 156/158/180. Preserve line-counter/IRQ/timer positions, actual frame completion and machine clocks. Document and test pending-row behavior at short/odd totals and runtime total/mode changes, retaining bounded progress and unvisited-row behavior. Test reset, restart, model changes, successful replacement and rejected loads for stale pipeline state.
- [ ] Add an original source-included CC0 cartridge that uses line polling and/or line IRQs to change shades and color palettes. Native and production-preview browser checks must compare resulting pixel rows against independent literals on all three models, including restart and fresh CPU-written execution markers. Extend existing fixture/browser tooling without another framework or proprietary assets.
- [ ] Preserve existing three-model gates, firmware-free startup, audio/PCM, GDMA/SDMA/Hyper Voice, SRAM/cartridge EEPROM/internal EEPROM, browser persistence, input, orientation and frame continuity. Keep device clocks independent of translation delay. Preserve browser-local ROM/save handling and ownership/provenance; introduce no copied emulator implementation or game-specific paths.
- [ ] Coordinator runs and records `python3 fixtures/build.py --check`, `python3 demo/build.py --check`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `git diff --check`. In `web`, run `npm run build:wasm`, `npm run build`, then complete `npm run test:browser` and `npm run test:compat` sequentially against production preview, including the new probe.
- [ ] Update hardware/LCD documentation, stale comments, fixture provenance and validation evidence. Record the original assumption, corrected requirement, source, rationale and remaining uncertainty. Coordinator reviews the final diff and actual results against every criterion before merge. Evidence-backed technical corrections require no human approval or independent AI re-review; preserve relevant acceptance rather than weakening it for incomplete code or failing checks.

## Optional validation

Compare additional lawful raster experiments or another browser engine. Report inspected source separately from executed results. Proprietary ROMs/firmware, physical consoles and human gameplay are unnecessary for acceptance.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WonderSwan-family hardware goal.
Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance criteria when primary hardware
specifications establish the correction. Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.
